transitions.transition_trigger: External verification against direct prior art (Narang 2018, Caruso 2023)
transitions.claim_before: Layer jamming for variable-stiffness continuum robots is a scientifically novel and defensible research direction.
transitions.threat: Direct prior art exists for laminar jamming stiffness models, friction-slip transitions, and experimental validation in soft machines.
transitions.counter_evidence: Narang et al. 2018 (Adv. Funct. Mater. 28, 1707136) and Caruso et al. 2023 (Int. J. Mech. Sci. 248, 108325) already solved laminar jamming modeling, slip onset, and hysteresis.
transitions.evidence_available_before: 54 seed papers in discovery corpus without integrated continuum layer-jamming beam model.
transitions.new_evidence: Narang 2018 and Caruso 2023 verified full text demonstrating analytical models, FEA, and experimental validation.
transitions.assumptions_before: Variable-stiffness layer jamming continuum robots lack predictive mechanics models in the literature.
transitions.assumptions_after: Broad architecture is uninventive; only specific unresolved mechanics limits (such as high-layer-count homogenized slip validity) could be novel.
transitions.decision: PIVOT: Falsify broad D1 claim; formulate provisional pivot candidate P1; mandate: DO NOT DEFEND P1, ATTACK IT WITH 2025-2026 LITERATURE.
transitions.scientific_consequence: Eliminated broad claim that layer jamming / variable stiffness continuum robots are novel in principle.
transitions.what_changed: Broad architecture novelty rejected; scope narrowed to mathematical modeling of homogenized slip in high-layer-count beams (P1).
transitions.what_did_not_change: Focus on layer jamming structures under vacuum confinement.

evidence_details.title: Mechanically Versatile Soft Machines through Laminar Jamming / Layer jamming: Modeling and experimental validation
evidence_details.what_the_evidence_proves: Laminar jamming stiffness modulation, friction-slip transitions, and experimental validation are well-established prior art.
evidence_details.what_the_evidence_does_not_prove: Does not prove that high-layer-count homogenized slip models have verified validity boundaries.

transitions.transition_trigger: Forward-citation discovery of Zhang et al. 2025 continuum beam model
transitions.claim_before: P1 candidate: Homogenized slip model for high-layer-count vacuum-jammed beams may possess an unresolved validity limit (or creating such a model is novel).
transitions.threat: Zhang et al. 2025 published a continuum-based model for layer jamming beams, deriving closed-form stress distributions and solving homogenized beam slip.
transitions.counter_evidence: Zhang et al. 2025 ('Toward a deeper understanding of layer jamming structures', Mech. Sci., 16, 821-2025) formulated the continuum beam slip model.
transitions.evidence_available_before: P1 hypothesis that homogenized slip continuum modeling remained open.
transitions.new_evidence: Zhang et al. 2025 full paper demonstrates closed-form sliding boundary quadratic approximation, Euler-Bernoulli extension, and iterative algorithm.
transitions.assumptions_before: Developing a homogenized continuum model for vacuum-jammed beam slip is an open research contribution.
transitions.assumptions_after: Model development is already solved by Zhang et al. 2025; research novelty cannot be in model formulation, but only in evaluating validity limits and breakdown boundaries.
transitions.decision: REFORMULATE: Adopt Zhang et al. 2025 as baseline model M1; evaluate validity breakdown limits instead of inventing M1.
transitions.scientific_consequence: Shifted thesis architecture from 'model development' to 'model validity / model-form error quantification' (M -> R -> E).
transitions.what_changed: Novelty locus migrated from model synthesis to model-form error quantification and breakdown domain mapping.
transitions.what_did_not_change: Target system remains vacuum-jammed beam with interlayer slip.

evidence_details.title: Toward a deeper understanding of layer jamming structures
evidence_details.what_the_evidence_proves: A continuum beam model for layer jamming with interlayer sliding boundary is formulated and experimentally tested.
evidence_details.what_the_evidence_does_not_prove: Does not prove where the continuum model breaks down across comprehensive parameter grids of layer count, vacuum, and curvature.

transitions.transition_trigger: D1-V003 validity gap search and cross-round synthesis
transitions.claim_before: Zhang et al. 2025 continuum model M1 validity limits are unexplored.
transitions.threat: Follow-up 2025-2026 papers (Zhang 2025b, Fan 2026) might have already characterized the validity limits of layer jamming continuum models.
transitions.counter_evidence: Semantic Scholar / forward citation screening showed Zhang 2025b (10.1007/s11465-025-0843-5) and Fan 2026 (10.1016/j.taml.2025.100633) focus on specific applications and control, not systematic model-form error boundaries.
transitions.new_evidence: Verified full-text analysis of forward citations confirms lack of systematic output-specific error maps across layer count and vacuum pressure.
transitions.assumptions_before: Validity limits can be claimed as a broad generic gap.
transitions.assumptions_after: Validity limits must be rigorously defined over an explicit 3-variable space (N x p_vac x kappa) with candidate claims C01-C04.
transitions.decision: NARROW: Formulate candidate claims C01-C04 around explicit 3-variable space (N x p_vac x kappa).
transitions.scientific_consequence: Defined concrete falsifiable candidate claims C01-C04.
transitions.what_changed: Generic validity claim replaced by parameterized domain (N x p_vac x kappa) and partitioned into subclaims C01-C04.
transitions.what_did_not_change: Focus on Zhang 2025 M1 model validity.

evidence_details.title: Forward citation corpus for Zhang et al. 2025
evidence_details.what_the_evidence_proves: Forward citations extend to control and dynamics but do not systematically quantify model-form error across N x p_vac x kappa.
evidence_details.what_the_evidence_does_not_prove: Does not prove absence of prior art in adjacent fields (composite beams, geology, contact mechanics).

transitions.transition_trigger: Adversarial audit against composite relative gradient theories
transitions.claim_before: C01: Discrete layer friction in vacuum jamming behaves distinctly from bonded composite relative gradient theories.
transitions.threat: Gradient elasticity and higher-order composite beam theories might account for interlayer sliding slip boundaries.
transitions.counter_evidence: 15 papers in gradient elasticity evaluated; composite beam models rely on continuous shear interaction without vacuum pressure coupling.
transitions.new_evidence: Full text of 15 gradient elasticity papers confirms lack of normal pressure confinement and unbonded Coulomb friction slip.
transitions.assumptions_before: Gradient theories might be mathematically equivalent to vacuum layer jamming.
transitions.assumptions_after: Gradient theories assume continuous interface cohesion; vacuum layer jamming requires discrete Coulomb slip with normal pressure coupling.
transitions.decision: NARROW: C01 narrowed to vacuum-confinement frictional contact.
transitions.scientific_consequence: Separated layer jamming mechanics from bonded composite gradient theories.
transitions.what_changed: C01 explicitly distinguished from cohesive shear interaction gradient beam models.
transitions.what_did_not_change: C01 hypothesis that discrete friction behaves distinctly from continuous gradient theory.

evidence_details.title: Composite gradient elasticity corpus
evidence_details.what_the_evidence_proves: Relative gradient elasticity theories do not incorporate vacuum-induced normal confinement or Coulomb slip.
evidence_details.what_the_evidence_does_not_prove: Does not address multi-layer partial interaction beam theory.

transitions.transition_trigger: Adversarial audit against multi-layered beam partial interaction models
transitions.claim_before: C02: Partial interaction beam models are predominantly 2-layer steel-concrete; multi-layer unbonded frictional contact remains open.
transitions.threat: Civil engineering partial-interaction composite beam models (Newmark-type) might have solved multi-layer friction slip.
transitions.counter_evidence: 16 papers on exact stiffness matrices audited; partial interaction literature focuses almost exclusively on 2-layer steel-concrete with constant-stiffness linear shear connectors.
transitions.new_evidence: Civil engineering literature corpus confirms lack of multi-layer unbonded frictional contact with pressure-dependent slip.
transitions.assumptions_before: Partial interaction theory might already encompass N-layer vacuum jamming.
transitions.assumptions_after: Partial interaction theory is limited to 2-layer linear shear connection; N-layer vacuum jamming requires non-linear unbonded contact.
transitions.decision: NARROW: C02 narrowed to multi-layer frictional contact with pressure-dependent slip.
transitions.scientific_consequence: Differentiated civil engineering 2-layer composite beams from N-layer vacuum jamming beams.
transitions.what_changed: C02 narrowed to exclude bonded/pinned shear connectors and focus on unbonded Coulomb friction.
transitions.what_did_not_change: C02 core proposition regarding partial interaction limitations.

evidence_details.title: Partial interaction composite beam corpus
evidence_details.what_the_evidence_proves: Partial interaction literature is predominantly 2-layer steel-concrete with discrete or smeared connectors.
evidence_details.what_the_evidence_does_not_prove: Does not evaluate microscopic contact mechanics or bolted joints.

transitions.transition_trigger: Adversarial audit against interface friction and bolted joint roughness models
transitions.claim_before: C03: Microscopic roughness contact redistribution does not provide closed continuum beam validity boundaries.
transitions.threat: Tribological roughness models and bolted joint fretting theories might predict continuum slip validity breakdown.
transitions.counter_evidence: 16 papers on microscopic joint contact audited; contact pressure redistribution models focus on local fretting and wear, not macroscopic beam-scale validity boundaries.
transitions.new_evidence: Joint friction corpus demonstrates microscopic contact models do not solve continuum beam validity boundaries.
transitions.assumptions_before: Microscopic joint contact theories might predict macroscopic beam validity limits.
transitions.assumptions_after: Microscopic models operate at asperities; beam-scale validity boundary is a macroscopic continuum mechanics question.
transitions.decision: NARROW: C03 narrowed to beam-scale contact mechanics.
transitions.scientific_consequence: Established that joint roughness theories do not pre-empt continuum beam validity maps.
transitions.what_changed: C03 scoped strictly to beam-scale macroscopic mechanics rather than microscopic asperity wear.
transitions.what_did_not_change: C03 focus on contact mechanics role in jamming breakdown.

evidence_details.title: Bolted joint interface friction corpus
evidence_details.what_the_evidence_proves: Microscopic joint roughness models address local stress concentrations and fretting rather than macroscopic beam validity.
evidence_details.what_the_evidence_does_not_prove: Does not check forward citations of Zhang 2025.

transitions.transition_trigger: Review of C04 focal paper tolerance semantics
transitions.claim_before: C04: Forward citations address multi-physics extensions; prior art supported a predeclared 5% acceptance tolerance.
transitions.threat: If prior art predeclared acceptance tolerances a priori, D1/M1's methodological rigor is not novel.
transitions.counter_evidence: Audit review in C04_SEMANTIC_CORRECTION.md showed focal paper ca46dc062d adopted a 5% error threshold post-hoc during inspection, NOT a priori.
transitions.evidence_available_before: Initial C04 audit assuming predeclared tolerance in paper ca46dc062d.
transitions.new_evidence: Verified full-text re-inspection of paper ca46dc062d confirming threshold was adopted post-hoc.
transitions.assumptions_before: Prior literature utilized predeclared acceptance tolerances.
transitions.assumptions_after: Prior literature relied on post-hoc error thresholds; predeclared tolerance is an unaddressed standard in prior art.
transitions.decision: CORRECT: Mark predeclared acceptance tolerance as unsupported in prior art; enforce a priori freeze in project governance (HG-06).
transitions.scientific_consequence: Corrected factual inaccuracy in C04 audit; established requirement for threshold freeze (HG-06).
transitions.what_changed: Semantic classification of tolerance in paper ca46dc062d changed from predeclared to post-hoc adopted.

evidence_details.title: Focal paper for C04 audit
evidence_details.what_the_evidence_proves: Focal paper uses an adopted 5% threshold post-hoc without a priori predeclaration.
evidence_details.what_the_evidence_does_not_prove: Does not prove that other literature predeclared acceptance thresholds.
